       - name: Checkout request target

-        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

-          ref: ${{ steps.target.outputs.ref }}

+        env:
+          TARGET_REPO: ${{ steps.target.outputs.repo }}
+          TARGET_REF: ${{ steps.target.outputs.ref }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          # Fetch only the reviewed head SHA and its ancestry from the head
+          # repo. A fetch-depth-0 checkout of a fork would fetch every branch
+          # and tag from an attacker-controlled repo, letting a fork exhaust
+          # runner disk or the 40-minute budget with blobs on unrelated refs.
+          # --filter=blob:none goes further: blobs materialize on demand
+          # for the checkout and the diff below, so blobs that exist only
+          # in intermediate commits (added then deleted, never in the
+          # final tree or the diff) are never downloaded at all.
+          # No credentials here: the repos are public and the fetch URL
+          # carries no token (the checkout this replaces used
+          # persist-credentials: false for the same reason).
+          if [[ -z "$TARGET_REPO" || -z "$TARGET_REF" ]]; then
+            echo "Missing checkout target" >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          git init -q -b main
+          git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${TARGET_REPO}.git" 2>/dev/null ||
+            git remote add origin "https://github.com/${TARGET_REPO}.git"
+          git fetch --no-tags --filter=blob:none origin "$TARGET_REF"
+          git -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout -q --detach FETCH_HEAD

@@ -284,12 +319,43 @@ jobs:
           # A pull request must not be able to rewrite the policy used to review itself.
           guide="$RUNNER_TEMP/REVIEWING.md"
           if [[ -n "$BASE_SHA" ]]; then
+            # The checkout is the (possibly fork) head repo, which may not
+            # contain the base SHA if main advanced since the PR opened.
+            # Fetch it from the trusted base repo (public read, no
+            # credentials). Best-effort: git show below is the gate, and
+            # the object is already present for same-repo PRs.
+            git fetch --no-tags "https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git" "$BASE_SHA" || true
             git show "$BASE_SHA:REVIEWING.md" > "$guide"
           else
             git show "HEAD:REVIEWING.md" > "$guide"
           fi
           test -s "$guide"
 
+      - name: Guard fetched size
+        if: steps.check_auth.outputs.authorized == 'true'
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          # Fail closed before any secret-holding step runs if the
+          # materialized checkout is far beyond a normal one (a .git of
+          # ~50 MiB plus a ~240 MiB working tree today). This counts both
+          # object storage and the working tree, where checkout duplicates
+          # materialized blobs. The time bound is the 40-minute job timeout.
+          # It deliberately runs after fetch/checkout rather than as a
+          # quota during materialization: GitHub-hosted runners are
+          # single-use, so exhaustion during fetch/checkout only fails
+          # this job (those steps fail before Codex runs), while a tmpfs
+          # remount of the workspace would risk breaking every review if
+          # the runner environment ever denies the mount. 2 GiB leaves
+          # ample headroom for legitimate growth.
+          max_kib=2097152
+          total_kib="$(du -sk . | cut -f1)"
+          git_kib="$(du -sk .git | cut -f1)"
+          echo "Materialized checkout: ${total_kib} KiB total (${git_kib} KiB .git), limit ${max_kib} KiB"
+          if (( total_kib > max_kib )); then
+            echo "::error title=Fetched size::Materialized checkout is ${total_kib} KiB, over the ${max_kib} KiB limit; refusing to review." >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
